what_its_for: Ticagrelor is a blood thinner that helps prevent blood clots from forming in your arteries. It is used to lower your risk of having a heart attack or stroke, especially if you have had a heart attack, unstable chest pain (unstable angina), or a procedure to open blocked arteries (like a stent placement). It works by stopping your blood platelets from sticking together and forming dangerous clots.
how_to_take: Take ticagrelor exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole or you can crush it and mix it with water if you have trouble swallowing. You may take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same two times every day (morning and evening). Do NOT stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can greatly increase your risk of a heart attack or blood clot. Most people take this along with low-dose aspirin (usually 75–100 mg daily). Do NOT take higher doses of aspirin (more than 100 mg per day) while on ticagrelor, as this can make the medicine less effective.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 180 mg (two 90 mg tablets) taken once as a loading dose, followed by 90 mg twice daily (morning and evening). After one year, your doctor may lower your dose to 60 mg twice daily if you are taking it for long-term heart protection. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose at the scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for the missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ticagrelor at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking aspirin at doses higher than 100 mg per day, as this reduces how well ticagrelor works. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating large amounts of grapefruit, as it can increase the amount of this drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid activities that could cause serious bleeding or injury (such as contact sports) while on this medicine. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are taking ticagrelor before any surgery, dental work, or medical procedures, since they may need to temporarily stop this medicine. Avoid starting new medicines, including over-the-counter products, herbal supplements, or vitamins, without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: unusual or prolonged bleeding (such as cuts that won't stop bleeding), coughing up blood, blood in your urine or stool (pink, red, or dark brown), vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, severe headache, dizziness, or sudden weakness (signs of bleeding in the brain), shortness of breath or difficulty breathing that is new or gets worse, chest pain, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel unusually dizzy, faint, or notice your heart beating slowly or irregularly.
when_it_works: Ticagrelor starts working within about 30 minutes to 2 hours after your first dose, so it begins protecting you quickly. However, it is important to keep taking it every day as prescribed — even if you feel well — because the protection against heart attacks and strokes depends on taking it consistently. Do not stop taking it without your doctor's guidance.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking ticagrelor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It may harm an unborn baby, especially during the last trimester, and it is not recommended during breastfeeding. Older adults (65 and older): No special dose adjustment is needed, but older adults may have a higher risk of bleeding, so report any unusual bleeding right away. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver problems: Ticagrelor should be used with caution if you have moderate to severe liver disease; talk to your doctor. Children: Ticagrelor is not approved for use in children.
